rationale: Bun delivers 30-50% real-world API throughput improvement over Node.js/Express. Cold start is 5-16x faster, critical for serverless/containerized deployments. CI test suite runs ~20x faster. Real migration cases confirm these gains (Trigger.dev 5x throughput, anonymous team p99 latency 180ms->65ms).
caveats: Synthetic 3x claims do not materialize in production
Upload performance is 3.5x worse than Node.js
HTTP pipelining is 5x worse than Node.js

rationale: The Zig-to-Rust rewrite (May 2026, ~960K lines) is the single largest signal of stability improvement but is days old with zero production track record. Pre-Rust Bun had confirmed memory leaks, segfaults on Linux/Docker, and OOM crashes under sustained load. The Rust rewrite likely fixes memory-leak-class bugs but introduces unknown regression risk from AI-generated code with ~13,000 unsafe blocks and insufficient human review.
evidence: Rust rewrite merged May 2026 (6,755 commits, 2,188 files)
caveats: Rust rewrite may close the stability gap entirely
Wait 1-2 release cycles for production feedback
Test suite pass rate encouraging but insufficient

rationale: Node.js API coverage is 95-98%. Express, Fastify, Hono, and Elysia all run on Bun. Native database clients (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Redis) are built-in and outperform npm equivalents. The critical blocker is native C/C++ addons -- sharp, bcrypt, canvas, argon2 are broken or unstable. Audit your dependency tree: <10 pure JS deps = safe, 1-3 native addons = parallel validate, >5 = defer.
evidence: Express +17% perf on Bun with zero changes
bun:sql native client 7.9x faster than ioredis
caveats: Native addon breakage is the #1 migration blocker
Prisma has connection pooling edge cases
socket.io requires WebSocket rewrite

rationale: No CVEs specific to the Bun runtime have been published. Bun has been weaponized by supply chain attackers (Shai-Hulud, Mini Shai-Hulud/SAP) as an alternative execution path that bypasses Node.js-focused controls. The PackageGate vulnerability (trustedDependencies bypass, Jan 2026) was patched quickly. The curl|bash install method lacks integrity verification. Mitigations exist (--ignore-scripts, lockfiles, digest-pinned Docker images).
evidence: Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud attack analyses
Datadog OTel instrumentation guide for unsupported runtimes
caveats: curl|bash install is an ongoing supply chain risk
Bun is an attractive attack vector because it bypasses Node.js-focused controls
No Bun-specific CVEs may indicate immaturity, not security

rationale: Datadog documents the OTel path for Bun explicitly (as 'Custom Components'). Traces and metrics work via OTLP HTTP export. Gaps: Bun.serve() and bun:sqlite require manual instrumentation; OTLP gRPC is unreliable; --inspect debugging is less polished than Node.js. Budget ~1-2 weeks to wire up production-grade observability.

rationale: Anthropic acquired Bun Dec 2025. MIT license persists. Anthropic's resources reduce abandonment risk but create vendor concentration if your stack is Bun + Claude Code + Anthropic API. The AI-assisted Rust rewrite demonstrates a development philosophy (fast, AI-driven, large-scale) that may not align with regulated-industry expectations for review and stability.
evidence: Rust rewrite completed in ~6 days via Claude Code
caveats: Vendor concentration if also using Claude Code + Anthropic API
Post-acquisition roadmap unclear
AI-driven development model may concern regulated industries

rationale: Bun-specific talent pool is small but Node.js developers adapt quickly (API surface is compatible). Deep Bun debugging expertise is rare. Learning curve is low for pure JS/TS; moderate when hitting Bun-specific edge cases. IDE integration and profiling tools are less mature than Node.js.
evidence: Community reports of ~20-25 hour debugging overhead over first 2-3 months

rationale: Bun crossed the production-readiness threshold for most API use cases in 2025-2026, but it is not a no-brainer drop-in replacement. The conditional path is: (1) audit native addon dependencies -- if >5, stay on Node.js; (2) if this is greenfield or zero native addons, adopt Bun with Hono or Elysia; (3) if migrating Express with 1-3 native addons, run parallel Node+Bun for 1-2 months; (4) wait 1-2 release cycles for the Rust rewrite to prove itself; (5) budget 1-2 weeks for observability setup and 2-3 weeks for migration. The Rust rewrite is promising but too new to bet production on without a parallel Node.js safety net.
